Bank of Canada Raises Policy Rate by 25 Basis Points to 2.5% in First Hike in Three Years

The Bank of Canada on October 28, 2026, raised its target for the overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.5%, the first increase since July 2023. The Bank Rate is now 2.75% and the deposit rate is 2.45%. The move aims to reduce the risk that persistently high energy prices spread to the prices of other goods and services. Fed Holds Rates Steady at 3.75%–4.00% in 10–2 Vote, Two Officials Favor Hike

The Federal Reserve voted 10–2 on October 28 to maintain the federal funds rate target range at 3.75%–4.00%. The FOMC said economic activity continues to expand at a strong pace, supported by resilient domestic spending, strong productivity growth, and robust capital investment, despite elevated geopolitical uncertainty. Job growth has kept pace with labor force growth, while unemployment has changed little. Inflation remains elevated, and the Committee will assess incoming data to determine the appropriate policy stance to return inflation to its 2% target. Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack dissented, favoring a 25-basis-point rate hike.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the central bank will vote on interest rates at seven of its eight scheduled policy meetings in 2027, reducing that number to six in 2028. The remaining meetings will focus on broader monetary policy discussions. — link
